$comment: The class features of the 5th edition SRD for the classes in play, by the hero level they come at (the Skills tab lists them above the cantrips). kind: passive (on from the level it comes at; a click on its box switches it off and on), active (put on the quick bar like a spell and used with the cast key; cooldown is its recovery in seconds) or info (a rule, a choice or a proficiency: nothing to switch). worked: false means the game does not play it out yet; it is listed with the rest and says so. needs: the id of a fighting style, a Fighter's Martial Archetype or a maneuver - only for a hero who chose it. unless: a choice (style_chosen, extra_style_chosen, archetype_chosen) that takes the feature off the list - the entry that asks for the choice goes once it is made, and the chosen style or archetype is listed in its place. replaces: the feature that this one takes the place of once it comes (Superior Critical is Improved Critical, better). uses: the hero levels at which an active has more uses (its cooldown is shared out among them). The Cleric's Divine Domain is Life and the Fiend is the Warlock's patron; the Fighter has all three Player's Handbook archetypes. Ability Score Improvements, fighting styles, the archetype, maneuvers and an Eldritch Knight's spells are chosen in the level panel.

fighter.name: Fighting Style
fighter.description: You adopt a style of fighting as your specialty: Archery, Defense, Dueling, Great Weapon Fighting, Protection or Two-Weapon Fighting. Pick it in the level panel (the badge by your level); you can't take the same style twice.

fighter.name: Archery
fighter.description: Your fighting style: +2 to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.

fighter.name: Defense
fighter.description: Your fighting style: +1 Armor Class while you are wearing armour.

fighter.name: Dueling
fighter.description: Your fighting style: +2 damage with a melee weapon held in one hand when you hold no other weapon (a shield is fine).

fighter.name: Great Weapon Fighting
fighter.description: Your fighting style: when you roll a 1 or a 2 on a damage die with a melee weapon held in two hands (a two-handed or versatile weapon), you roll that die again and must use the new roll.

fighter.name: Two-Weapon Fighting
fighter.description: Your fighting style: when you fight with a weapon in each hand, you add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.

fighter.name: Protection
fighter.description: While you carry a shield, an enemy's attack on an ally within 5 feet of you is rolled with disadvantage. It needs 5 seconds to recover.

fighter.name: Second Wind
fighter.description: You draw on your stamina to heal yourself for 1d10 + your fighter level. In the tabletop game it recovers with a short or long rest; here it recovers in 30 seconds, and a rest restores it at once.

fighter.name: Action Surge
fighter.description: You push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment: every other ability and spell on your quick bar is ready again at once. In the tabletop game it recovers with a rest (two uses from level 17, one a turn); here it recovers in 60 seconds, 30 from level 17.

fighter.name: Martial Archetype
fighter.description: You choose an archetype that you strive to emulate in your combat styles and techniques: the Champion, the Battle Master or the Eldritch Knight. Pick it in the level panel (the tab of level 3). It gives you features at levels 3, 7, 10, 15 and 18.

fighter.name: Champion
fighter.description: Your Martial Archetype: the archetype of raw physical power honed to deadly perfection. Your weapon attacks are critical hits more often, you are a remarkable athlete, you take a second fighting style at level 10 and from level 18 you mend yourself as you fight on.

fighter.name: Battle Master
fighter.description: Your Martial Archetype: a student of the art of war. Superiority dice fuel maneuvers that trip, push, disarm, goad and frighten foes, parry blows, strike back and rally allies.

fighter.name: Eldritch Knight
fighter.description: Your Martial Archetype: martial prowess joined to wizard magic. You cast abjuration and evocation spells with Intelligence, strike with your weapon as you cast, mark foes so they resist your spells worse, and step through the air with Action Surge.

fighter.name: Improved Critical
fighter.description: Your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

fighter.name: Combat Superiority
fighter.description: You learn maneuvers that are fueled by special dice called superiority dice. You have 4 superiority dice (d8), a fifth at level 7 and a sixth at level 15; you know 3 maneuvers, 5 from level 7, 7 from level 10 and 9 from level 15. A maneuver is readied from the quick bar and spends a die when it is used; a rest brings the dice back. The saving throw some maneuvers ask is 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (the better one).

fighter.name: Student of War
fighter.description: You gain proficiency with one type of artisan's tools of your choice.

fighter.name: Commander's Strike
fighter.description: Maneuver. You forgo a blow to direct an ally: the nearest other hero within 30 feet deals a superiority die more damage with their next weapon hit. It needs another hero close by.

fighter.name: Disarming Attack
fighter.description: Maneuver. Your next weapon hit deals a superiority die more damage, and the foe makes a Strength saving throw against your maneuver DC or drops its weapon: it fights bare-handed from then on.

fighter.name: Distracting Strike
fighter.description: Maneuver. Your next weapon hit deals a superiority die more damage, and the next attack on that foe by someone else has advantage until its distraction wears off.

fighter.name: Evasive Footwork
fighter.description: Maneuver. You roll a superiority die and add it to your Armor Class for 10 seconds, but only while you are moving.

fighter.name: Feinting Attack
fighter.description: Maneuver. You feint: your next weapon attack has advantage, and a hit deals a superiority die more damage.

fighter.name: Goading Attack
fighter.description: Maneuver. Your next weapon hit deals a superiority die more damage, and the foe makes a Wisdom saving throw against your maneuver DC or has disadvantage on attacks against anyone but you for a while.

fighter.name: Lunging Attack
fighter.description: Maneuver. Your next melee swing reaches 5 feet further, and a hit deals a superiority die more damage.

fighter.name: Maneuvering Attack
fighter.description: Maneuver. Your next weapon hit deals a superiority die more damage, and a friendly creature that can see or hear you moves up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks from the foe (nothing in this game makes an opportunity attack, so the damage is all you see).

fighter.name: Menacing Attack
fighter.description: Maneuver. Your next weapon hit deals a superiority die more damage, and the foe makes a Wisdom saving throw against your maneuver DC or is frightened of you for a while: it attacks with disadvantage.

fighter.name: Parry
fighter.description: Maneuver. You ready yourself for 10 seconds: when a foe's melee attack hurts you, the damage is reduced by a superiority die + your Dexterity modifier.

fighter.name: Precision Attack
fighter.description: Maneuver. You ready yourself for 10 seconds: when one of your weapon attacks misses, a superiority die is added to its roll, and if that makes it hit the die is spent.

fighter.name: Pushing Attack
fighter.description: Maneuver. Your next weapon hit deals a superiority die more damage, and the foe (Large or smaller) makes a Strength saving throw against your maneuver DC or is pushed up to 15 feet away.

fighter.name: Rally
fighter.description: Maneuver. The nearest other hero within 30 feet gains temporary hit points equal to a superiority die + your Charisma modifier. It needs another hero close by.

fighter.name: Riposte
fighter.description: Maneuver. You ready yourself for 10 seconds: when a foe misses you with a melee attack, you strike back at once with a weapon attack that deals a superiority die more damage on a hit.

fighter.name: Sweeping Attack
fighter.description: Maneuver. When your next melee swing hits, another foe within 5 feet of the first and within your reach takes damage equal to a superiority die, if your attack roll would hit it too.

fighter.name: Trip Attack
fighter.description: Maneuver. Your next weapon hit deals a superiority die more damage, and the foe (Large or smaller) makes a Strength saving throw against your maneuver DC or is knocked prone: attacks on it have advantage, and its own have disadvantage.

fighter.name: Spellcasting
fighter.description: You augment your martial prowess with the ability to cast wizard spells, with Intelligence. You learn 2 cantrips and 3 spells at level 3 and more as you grow (3 cantrips from level 10, 13 spells at level 20), and open spell levels 1 to 4 at levels 3, 7, 13 and 19. Your spells are abjuration or evocation, except one at each of levels 3, 8, 14 and 20. Choose them in the level panel; point at a spell to read it.

fighter.name: Weapon Bond
fighter.description: You learn a ritual that creates a magical bond between yourself and one weapon. You can't be disarmed of that weapon unless you are incapacitated, and if it is on the same plane of existence, you can summon it as a bonus action on your turn, causing it to teleport instantly to your hand.

fighter.name: Extra Attack
fighter.description: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action: a swing strikes twice in a row, or two arrows fly one after the other. Three attacks at level 11, four at level 20.

fighter.name: Remarkable Athlete
fighter.description: You can add half your proficiency bonus (rounded up) to any Strength, Dexterity or Constitution check you make that doesn't already use your proficiency bonus: here that is your initiative. In addition, when you make a running long jump, the distance you can cover increases by a number of feet equal to your Strength modifier (there are no jumps in this game).

fighter.name: Know Your Enemy
fighter.description: If you spend at least 1 minute observing or interacting with another creature outside combat, you can learn certain information about its capabilities compared to your own: whether it is your equal, superior or inferior in two characteristics of your choice (Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Armor Class, current hit points, total class levels or fighter levels).

fighter.name: War Magic
fighter.description: When you cast a cantrip, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action: a swing or a shot follows at once.

fighter.name: Indomitable
fighter.description: You can reroll a saving throw that you fail, and must use the new roll. Two uses from level 13, three from level 17; in the tabletop game they come back with a long rest. Nothing in this dungeon makes a hero roll a saving throw yet, so it has nothing to reroll for now.

fighter.name: Additional Fighting Style
fighter.description: You can choose a second option from the Fighting Style class feature (you can't take the same style twice). Pick it in the level panel (the tab of level 10).

fighter.name: Improved Combat Superiority
fighter.description: Your superiority dice turn into d10s. At level 18, they turn into d12s.

fighter.name: Eldritch Strike
fighter.description: You learn how to make your weapon strikes undercut a creature's resistance to your spells: when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, that creature has disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes against a spell you cast within the next 6 seconds.

fighter.name: Superior Critical
fighter.description: Your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 18, 19 or 20.

fighter.name: Relentless
fighter.description: When you roll initiative and have no superiority dice remaining, you regain 1 superiority die.

fighter.name: Arcane Charge
fighter.description: You gain the ability to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see when you use your Action Surge: you step through the air towards where you aim.

fighter.name: Survivor
fighter.description: You attain the pinnacle of resilience in battle. At the start of each of your turns (every 6 seconds here), you regain hit points equal to 5 + your Constitution modifier if you have no more than half of your hit points left. You don't gain this benefit if you have 0 hit points.

fighter.name: Improved War Magic
fighter.description: When you cast a spell, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action: a swing or a shot follows at once.

wizard.name: Spellcasting
wizard.description: You cast wizard spells with Intelligence. You learn more spells and open higher spell levels as you gain levels.

wizard.name: Arcane Recovery
wizard.description: You regain your focus: every spell on your quick bar is ready to cast again at once. In the tabletop game it is once a day, on a short rest; here it recovers in 2 minutes.

wizard.name: Spell Mastery
wizard.description: Choose a 1st-level and a 2nd-level wizard spell. You can cast them at their lowest level without expending a spell slot.

wizard.name: Signature Spells
wizard.description: Choose two 3rd-level wizard spells as your signature spells. You can cast each once at 3rd level without expending a spell slot.

rogue.name: Expertise
rogue.description: Choose two of your skill proficiencies: your proficiency bonus is doubled for them. Two more at level 6.

rogue.name: Sneak Attack
rogue.description: +1d6 damage with a finesse or ranged weapon, one more die every two levels (the tabletop rule asks for advantage or an ally beside the target; in a real-time fight every such blow counts).

rogue.name: Thieves' Cant
rogue.description: You know the secret mix of dialect, jargon and code that lets you hide messages in seemingly normal conversation.

rogue.name: Cunning Action
rogue.description: Your quick thinking lets you Dash as a bonus action: your sprint stamina is full again at once.

rogue.name: Uncanny Dodge
rogue.description: When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack's damage against you.

rogue.name: Evasion
rogue.description: When you are subjected to an effect that allows a Dexterity saving throw for half damage, you take no damage if you succeed, and only half if you fail.

rogue.name: Reliable Talent
rogue.description: Whenever you make an ability check that lets you add your proficiency bonus, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

rogue.name: Blindsense
rogue.description: If you are able to hear, you are aware of the location of any hidden or invisible creature within 10 feet of you.

rogue.name: Slippery Mind
rogue.description: You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws.

rogue.name: Elusive
rogue.description: No attack roll has advantage against you while you aren't incapacitated.

rogue.name: Stroke of Luck
rogue.description: If your attack misses a target within range, you can turn the miss into a hit. Alternatively, when you fail an ability check, you can treat the d20 roll as a 20.

warlock.name: Pact Magic
warlock.description: You cast warlock spells with Charisma. Your slots are few but always cast at your highest slot level (up to 5th); a short rest restores them. Your patron is the Fiend.

warlock.name: Eldritch Invocations
warlock.description: You gain eldritch invocations, fragments of forbidden knowledge that imbue you with an abiding magical ability. More at levels 5, 7, 9, 12, 15 and 18.

warlock.name: Agonizing Blast
warlock.description: Eldritch Blast adds your Charisma modifier to its damage.

warlock.name: Pact Boon
warlock.description: Your patron grants you a gift: the Pact of the Chain, the Blade or the Tome.

warlock.name: Mystic Arcanum
warlock.description: Your patron grants you a magical secret: a 6th-level spell, learnt at level 11. A 7th-level spell follows at level 13, an 8th at level 15 and a 9th at level 17. Each is cast at its own level only.

warlock.name: Eldritch Master
warlock.description: You can draw on your inner reserve of mystical power: every spell on your quick bar is ready to cast again at once. In the tabletop game it takes a minute of entreating your patron, once a day; here it recovers in 2 minutes.

bard.name: Spellcasting
bard.description: You cast bard spells with Charisma. You learn more spells and open higher spell levels as you gain levels.

bard.name: Bardic Inspiration
bard.description: You can inspire others through stirring words or music: an ally adds a d6 to one attack roll, ability check or saving throw. The die grows to d8 at level 5, d10 at level 10 and d12 at level 15.

bard.name: Jack of All Trades
bard.description: Half your proficiency bonus (rounded down) is added to initiative.

bard.name: Song of Rest
bard.description: Allies who regain hit points at the end of a short rest recover an extra 1d6. The die grows to d8 at level 9, d10 at level 13 and d12 at level 17.

bard.name: Expertise
bard.description: Choose two of your skill proficiencies: your proficiency bonus is doubled for them. Two more at level 10.

bard.name: Font of Inspiration
bard.description: You regain all of your expended uses of Bardic Inspiration when you finish a short or long rest.

bard.name: Countercharm
bard.description: You can use musical notes or words of power to disrupt mind-influencing effects: you and nearby allies have advantage on saving throws against being frightened or charmed.

bard.name: Magical Secrets
bard.description: You have plundered magical knowledge from a wide spectrum of disciplines: you can learn spells from any class's list.

bard.name: Superior Inspiration
bard.description: When you roll initiative and have no uses of Bardic Inspiration left, you regain one use.

cleric.name: Spellcasting
cleric.description: You cast cleric spells with Wisdom. You learn more spells and open higher spell levels as you gain levels. Your Divine Domain is Life.

cleric.name: Disciple of Life
cleric.description: Your healing spells mend 2 + the spell's level more.

cleric.name: Channel Divinity: Preserve Life
cleric.description: You present your holy symbol and evoke healing energy: a pool of 5 x your cleric level in hit points is shared among the allies within 30 feet (yourself included), none above half their hit points. In the tabletop game it recovers with a rest; here in 30 seconds.

cleric.name: Destroy Undead
cleric.description: When an undead fails its saving throw against your Turn Undead feature, it is instantly destroyed if its challenge rating is at or below a threshold: 1/2 at level 5, 1 at 8, 2 at 11, 3 at 14 and 4 at 17.

cleric.name: Blessed Healer
cleric.description: When you cast a spell that restores hit points to another creature, you regain 2 + the spell's level hit points yourself.

cleric.name: Divine Strike
cleric.description: Your weapon strikes are infused with divine energy: +1d8 radiant damage with a weapon, 2d8 from level 14.

cleric.name: Divine Intervention
cleric.description: You can call on your deity to intervene on your behalf when your need is great.

cleric.name: Supreme Healing
cleric.description: When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell, you instead use the highest number possible for each die.
